decisions.title: ownership-based middle class as organizing identity
decisions.question: Should the book’s organizing identity be framed as a shift from a wage-based to an ownership-based middle class, while keeping the canonical definition unchanged?
decisions.rationale: Strong candidate identity from post-Phase-1 strategic direction. Must remain distinct from overclaiming national greatness.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as working organizing thesis; keep canonical definition stable.

decisions.title: Part VI title and chapter expansion
decisions.question: Should Part VI be retitled Transition, Testing, and National Transformation and expanded with First 100 Days / multi-horizon / failure / living-constitution emphases while preserving stable chapter IDs?
decisions.rationale: Existing Part VI already covers transition; proposed structure deepens testing and impact analysis.
decisions.recommendation: Keep IDs; refine titles/briefs; add units only if necessary.

decisions.title: Constitutional Capitalism Institute
decisions.question: Should the project add a fourth component — the Constitutional Capitalism Institute — for modeling, scenarios, critiques, and revision cycles?
decisions.rationale: Reinforces evolving research framework rather than static ideology.
decisions.recommendation: Approve as planned domain; defer full app until Phase 2/5 readiness.

decisions.title: public prediction ranges
decisions.question: May public pages use illustrative ranges (e.g., – labor-tax relief examples) if clearly labeled as non-modeled illustrations?
decisions.rationale: Useful for intuition; high misuse risk if presented as forecasts.
decisions.recommendation: Allow only with prominent prediction/illustration labels; no GDP/wealth certainty claims.

decisions.title: three parallel books
decisions.question: Should the project develop as three parallel books — public manuscript, Evidence Companion, and Implementation Manual — rather than one overloaded manuscript?
decisions.rationale: Keeps Book One readable while building rigor and implementation pathways without pretending source verification or modeling are done.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as working architecture; keep Book One title/subtitle unchanged.

decisions.title: Constitutional Capitalism Test
decisions.question: Should the ten-question Constitutional Capitalism Test become a defining policy screen for laws, regulations, taxes, subsidies, and reforms?
decisions.rationale: Shifts debate from preference to principle-consistency and forces measurability.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as proposed project standard; do not present as enacted constitutional law.

decisions.title: chapter evaluation closing template
decisions.question: Should every developed chapter end with Success Metrics, Risks, Counterarguments, Pilot Test, Constitutional Questions, Research Still Needed, International Examples, and Impact Timeline?
decisions.rationale: Makes the philosophy measurable and honest about uncertainty across ~90 units.
impact: Book One readability vs rigor balance
decisions.recommendation: Require the block from researching/drafting onward; stubs allowed earlier.

decisions.title: National Baseline as Phase 2 center
decisions.question: Should Phase 2 center on building a National Baseline/dashboard — pre-committing to success measures — rather than only gathering diagnosis research notes?
decisions.rationale: Evidence-building and honest evaluation require knowing what would count as success before conclusions harden.
decisions.recommendation: Reframe Phase 2 as evidence + National Baseline; diagnosis research continues inside that frame.

decisions.title: sacred sentence on power flow
decisions.question: Should the never-changing sacred sentence be: "Power should always flow toward the people, never permanently away from them."?
decisions.rationale: Gives every institution a single constitutional test question.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as working sacred sentence; keep distinct from canonical definition until formal amendment.

decisions.title: website as primary living medium
decisions.question: Should the Constitutional Capitalism Project treat the living website as the primary medium and the book as an Introduction, rather than containing the philosophy only in a static book?
decisions.rationale: Enables branching domains, life-path views, research, pilots, and amendments.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt living-project architecture; keep title/subtitle stable.

decisions.title: subsidiarity acknowledgement and extension
decisions.question: Should the philosophy explicitly acknowledge subsidiarity as a shared intuition and adopt the working statement extending it to authority, ownership, and economic benefit?
decisions.rationale: Avoids false novelty claims while clarifying economic extension.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt acknowledgement + working statement as draft principle.

decisions.title: stewardship as fifth pillar
decisions.question: Should Stewardship join Liberty, Ownership, Accountability, and Prosperity as a fifth core pillar?
decisions.rationale: Adds multi-generational horizon beyond current prosperity.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as proposed pillar.

decisions.title: permanent ownership and tax-shift agenda
decisions.question: Should permanent ownership security and shifting away from labor/property taxes that erode ownership become a formal design agenda (not yet locked policy)?
decisions.rationale: Radical aspiration requiring honest local-funding and revenue redesign before prescription.
decisions.recommendation: Accept as open design agenda; forbid presenting as solved policy.

decisions.title: people as source framing with dignity guardrail
decisions.question: Should the first principle state that people are the nation's greatest source of productive capacity while forbidding "mere resource" language?
decisions.rationale: Keeps human investment productive without instrumentalizing persons.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt first-principle text + dignity guardrail.

decisions.title: duty of constructive improvement
decisions.question: Should a Constitutional Duty of Improvement — questioning and improving the system through evidence and constitutional process — become a core article/principle?
decisions.rationale: Makes Living Amendments and critique a civic virtue rather than disloyalty.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as draft principle and deepen Article XII.

decisions.title: community economic sovereignty article emphasis
decisions.question: Should Community Economic Sovereignty become a pillar-level emphasis under Communities and Local Economies (Article VIII)?
decisions.rationale: Captures resilience, food/energy/education/health capacity, and belonging without secession claims.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt emphasis; keep political sovereignty language out.

decisions.title: essential infrastructure accessibility principle
decisions.question: Should essential infrastructure accessibility (e.g., transportation and broadband as candidate arteries) be adopted as a principle while leaving public/private/hybrid models open?
decisions.rationale: Separates principle from ownership model; supports distributed prosperity.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt principle; require local model analysis before mandates.

decisions.title: justice as principal developing doctrine
decisions.question: Should Justice, Safety, and Restoration be adopted as developing doctrine (CC-DEV-011–014) and a full Phase 2 research domain before detailed justice policy is written?
decisions.rationale: Justice is the mechanism that determines whether liberty, ownership, opportunity, and accountability are real. Doctrine and research architecture must precede legislation.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; block detailed justice policy until sourced diagnosis modules exist.

decisions.title: Justice Safety and Restoration website domain
decisions.question: Should Justice, Safety, and Restoration become a principal living-website domain with the listed branches and Justice Test?
decisions.rationale: Places justice at website IA level equal to economics and flourishing, with branch structure for long-term school-of-thought depth.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish branch pages only as research matures.

decisions.title: democracy as second constitutional spine
decisions.question: Should Democracy, Representation, and Distributed Government become a second constitutional spine (CC-DEV-015–019) and full Phase 2 research domain before detailed political-structure policy?
decisions.rationale: Economic power returned to the people is incomplete if political power remains self-protecting through districts, parties, procedure, donors, and unified government.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; block detailed election/redistricting legislation until sourced diagnosis modules exist.

decisions.title: Democracy Representation and Distributed Government website domain
decisions.question: Should the living-website Democracy node expand to Democracy, Representation, and Distributed Government with the listed branches, Democracy Test, and Bill Transparency Test?
decisions.rationale: Places political-power distribution at website IA level equal to economics and justice.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish branch pages only as research matures.

decisions.title: public service and institutional modernization doctrine
decisions.question: Should Government Capacity, Public Service, and Institutional Modernization become developing doctrine (CC-DEV-020–024) and a full Phase 2 research domain before detailed administrative legislation?
decisions.rationale: Justice and democracy spines fail in practice if agencies and boards are opaque, captured, digitally exclusive, or administratively exhausting. Public service is stewardship of a public trust.
impact: Arkansas Public Authority Inventory design agenda
Arkansas Civic Service Credential design agenda
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; block detailed civil-service/IT/board packages until sourced diagnosis modules exist.

decisions.title: Public Service and the 21st-Century State website domain
decisions.question: Should the living-website Government node become Public Service and the 21st-Century State with the listed branches and Government Capacity Test?
decisions.rationale: Places institutional modernization at website IA level equal to justice and democracy spines.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish branch pages only as research matures.

decisions.title: friction reduction as defining public-service doctrine
decisions.question: Should Constitutional Capitalism elevate administrative friction reduction — invisible bureaucracy with never-unaccountable power; government-as-platform; collect-once; citizen-experience metrics; Regulation Reason Test; assistive AI with human final judgment — as defining developing doctrine (CC-DEV-025–028)?
decisions.rationale: The defining design question is not more vs less government, but better outcomes with fewer layers, less friction, and greater accountability. This distinguishes lean constitutional government from both shrink-until-broken and bureaucracy-for-its-own-sake.
impact: iconic phrase: Government should become invisible—but never unaccountable
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as defining institutional design doctrine; keep Arkansas inventory/credential as design agendas; do not invent 80/20 statistics or board counts; block detailed IT/civil-service statutes until Phase 2.1 sourcing.

decisions.title: constitutional transparency and People's Ledger doctrine
decisions.question: Should Constitutional Transparency and the People's Ledger become developing doctrine (CC-DEV-029–032) and a full Phase 2 research domain — presumption of openness with legitimate exceptions, not absolute disclosure?
decisions.rationale: Invisible-but-never-unaccountable government requires reviewable information held in trust. Openness by presumption with narrow, lawful, reviewable exceptions protects both accountability and rights.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; treat People's Ledger as design agenda; do not invent FOIA/portal statistics; block detailed open-records legislation until sourced diagnosis.

decisions.title: Constitutional Transparency website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website add Constitutional Transparency and the People's Ledger as a seeded domain with branches and the Constitutional Transparency Test?
decisions.rationale: Places transparency at website IA level equal to justice, democracy, and public-service spines.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish branch pages only as research matures.

decisions.title: essential systems design doctrine
decisions.question: Should banking, insurance, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, community health, and prevention become an Essential Systems developing doctrine (CC-DEV-033–037) framed as incentive and system design rather than inherent corruption?
decisions.rationale: Essential industries belong in the philosophy, but persuasion and rigor require shared constitutional questions, four-question chapter methods, and measurable tests — leaving room for evidence to refine conclusions.
impact: links to banking and healthcare diagnosis briefs
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; block detailed sector legislation until sourced diagnosis; forbid unsupported systemic-intent claims about pharmaceuticals or other industries.

decisions.title: Essential Systems website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website add Essential Systems as a major seeded domain with banking, insurance, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, Community Health Index, and preventive-society branches?
decisions.rationale: Gives readers a shared structure to reason through essential industries before reforms, elevating healthcare and related systems beyond a single proposed node.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish industry branch pages only as research matures.

decisions.title: Human Capital Doctrine and regional academy pilot posture
decisions.question: Should Human Capital Infrastructure become developing doctrine (CC-DEV-038–041), with regional civic/innovation academies treated as a researchable pilot model of equal-dignity pathways rather than a locked statewide design?
decisions.rationale: Investing in capable citizens fits rural strength, productive capacity, ownership, families, and local leadership. Pilots and evidence must precede statewide lock-in; pathways must carry equal dignity.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt doctrine and architecture; keep academy names and regional maps illustrative; block statewide academy statute until sourced diagnosis and pilot design; do not invent outcomes or treat ASMSA as evaluated proof in this slice.

decisions.title: Human Capital Doctrine website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website add Human Capital Doctrine as a major seeded domain, elevating education into human-capital infrastructure with regional academy branches?
decisions.rationale: Makes human infrastructure a first-class public surface equal to Essential Systems and institutional spines.
decisions.recommendation: Seed domain and public doctrine page; publish branch pages only as research and pilots mature.

decisions.title: playbooks and Community Operating System architecture
decisions.question: Should Constitutional Capitalism adopt playbooks, a seven-layer living architecture, community asset-first blueprints, and a permanent Implementation Completeness Rule as developing doctrine (CC-DEV-042–045), with the Community OS treated as a design agenda rather than an operating product?
decisions.rationale: The movement becomes practical when every idea can answer how a real community begins and how success is measured. Same principles; adaptive local implementation.
impact: links to Implementation Manual and pilots
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; keep Community OS and roadmap generator as design agendas; do not invent town growth outcomes; AI organizes best practices only.

decisions.title: Build Your Community website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website seed Build Your Community as the public surface for playbooks, asset inventories, prosperity-plan stages, and Community OS design?
decisions.rationale: Gives visitors a practical entry equal to institutional doctrine pages while remaining honest that the OS is not yet an operating product.
decisions.recommendation: Seed doctrine page and architecture; ship interactive roadmap tools only after product design, security, and sourced playbook modules exist.

decisions.title: Community Safety and Restoration System
decisions.question: Should Justice, Safety, and Restoration be elevated from isolated police/prison reforms into a complete Community Safety and Restoration System — Community Safety Corps, public corrections without confinement-profit incentives, decision pathways A–E, secure restoration campuses, reentry from day one, Restoration Councils, and automatic transparency — as developing doctrine (CC-DEV-046–049) with the public domain titled Community Safety, Justice, and Restoration?
decisions.rationale: Public safety belongs to the community. The objective is more safety and restoration with far less permanent discarding of human potential — not merely softer or tougher on crime. Armed officers should not be the default for every social, health, and administrative problem.
impact: website domain retitle Community Safety, Justice, and Restoration
Justice Test updates for least-coercive response and confinement profit
decisions.recommendation: Adopt complete-system architecture; keep Community Safety Corps and Restoration Councils as design agendas; correct private-prison federal timeline (2016 Yates; 2017 Sessions rescission); do not invent crime or recidivism statistics; keep detailed statutes blocked until Phase 2.1 sourcing.

decisions.title: Permanent Public Safety System
decisions.question: Should Constitutional Capitalism reject any category of citizens unworthy of reentry and instead adopt a Permanent Public Safety System — humane permanent incapacitation with continuing review through publicly operated Secure Public Safety Campuses, graduated custody, periodic dangerousness review, productive contribution without private enrichment, resource concentration, rejection of exile, and anti-misuse safeguards — as developing doctrine (CC-DEV-050–052)?
decisions.rationale: Dignity forbids declaring people permanently beyond value. Public safety still requires an honest answer for continuing extreme danger after due process and repeated review: public, humane, productive, reviewable secure custody — not abandonment, private imprisonment, or punishment colonies.
impact: website branches Secure Public Safety Campuses / Permanent Public Safety System
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as design agenda within the Community Safety system; keep Secure Public Safety Campuses as architecture not operating facilities; complete Eighth Amendment legal-review package before statutes; attribute aging misconduct/rearrest to DOJ OIG (not GAO-17-379 alone); do not invent custody statistics.

decisions.title: Resource Sovereignty and Community Stewardship doctrine
decisions.question: Should Resource Sovereignty and Community Stewardship become central developing doctrine (CC-DEV-053–057) — Community Resource Compacts, progressive pricing, Community Resource Dividend and equity, sector compacts, Resource and Pollution Ledger, Local Carbon Restoration Exchange, community-owned energy, and household energy floor — before detailed resource statutes?
decisions.rationale: Natural resources belong first to the place that bears extraction, consumption, congestion, pollution, and long-term risk. Permits must not convert community inheritance into free private inputs. The greater the consumption, scarcity, risk, or damage, the greater the obligation to the affected community.
decisions.recommendation: Adopt architecture and doctrine; keep Compacts, Ledger, and Exchange as design agendas; treat illustrative dividend percentages as modeling targets not locked rates; note GHGRP political changeability; do not invent resource or carbon statistics.

decisions.title: Resource Sovereignty website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website seed Resource Sovereignty and Community Stewardship as the public Environment domain surface (CC-WEB-ENVIRONMENT) with Community Resource Compact architecture and Carrying-Capacity Test?
decisions.rationale: Gives visitors a coherent public entry for place-based resource rights, progressive pricing, dividends, data-center/mining/warehouse rules, and regenerative restoration without pretending operating products already exist.
decisions.recommendation: Seed doctrine page and architecture; publish interactive calculators or exchanges only after product design, security, and sourced modules exist.

decisions.title: Community Food Security System doctrine
decisions.question: Should Constitutional Capitalism broaden food architecture from a single food-network idea into a Community Food Security System (CC-DEV-058–061) that treats food as critical infrastructure, prioritizes local capacity while retaining broader trade, rejects export-only mass-production rules, and includes Regional Networks, a State Food Exchange, waste reduction, reserves, regenerative links, education, and a dashboard?
decisions.rationale: Local food strength without isolation. Large-scale agriculture and trade stabilize supply when local harvests fail; communities still need capacity, processing, reserves, and measurable improvement.
impact: links to Resource Sovereignty regenerative payments and Human Capital education
decisions.recommendation: Adopt as broad testable system architecture; keep Network/Exchange/Dashboard/Reserves as design agendas; do not invent local-sourcing or waste statistics; reject export-only staple principle.

decisions.title: Community Food Security website domain
decisions.question: Should the living website seed Community Food Security System as the public Agriculture domain surface (CC-WEB-AGRICULTURE) at /food-security/?
decisions.rationale: Gives visitors a coherent public entry for food-as-infrastructure, Local First/Export Second, regional logistics, and measurable resilience without pretending operating products already exist.
decisions.recommendation: Seed doctrine page; ship marketplace software only after product design, security, and sourced modules exist.
